name: snow
desc: Whitespace steganography: coded messages using whitespace
why: Hides messages in trailing whitespace, a steganography trick most developers have never encountered and can poke at in minutes.

brief.what_it_is: SNOW is a command-line steganography tool that hides a message inside ASCII text by appending spaces and tabs to the ends of lines. The hidden data is invisible in a normal text viewer, and the tool can optionally encrypt it with the built-in ICE algorithm. The homepage describes it as the Steganographic Nature Of Whitespace, and it ships as C source, DOS/Windows executables, and a Java version.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a way to conceal messages so that casual observers cannot see them, with encryption as a second layer if the message is detected.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says the message is encoded by appending whitespace to the end of lines of ASCII text. Because spaces and tabs are not visible in most viewers, the payload is hidden in plain sight. The separate 'How it works' page was linked but not fetched, so the exact encoding scheme is not described here.
brief.install_notes: Source is distributed as snow-20130616.tar.gz or snow.zip, so building from source is needed for Unix. Prebuilt options include snwdos16.zip and snwdos32.zip for DOS/Windows and a Java 1.1 jar/applet. The Java applet needs a Java 1.1-capable browser. The homepage notes a 1998 fix so that Unix builds can read DOS-concealed files, and that DOS and other versions are now compatible on encryption. No Homebrew-specific steps were seen.
brief.standout: It hides data in trailing whitespace, which most developers have never looked at, and it pairs that with a real cipher (ICE) so the message stays unreadable even if someone spots the whitespace. The homepage also links a JavaScript implementation and a CGI script that hides messages inside HTML pages.
brief.status: quiet. The homepage was last modified 9 November 2025, but the newest downloadable source is dated 16 June 2013 and the license change was dated the same day. No release notes or commit history were checked.
brief.caveats: The homepage text returned to me had no link targets, so the manual page, 'How it works', logo page, and example links could not be followed or verified. The license is Apache 2.0 as of 2013. The homepage also contains a 1998 history of encryption bugs that were fixed. The project is old and the only maintained-looking signal is the page edit date.

entry.title: snow
entry.tldr: Hides a message in the invisible spaces and tabs at the ends of lines of ordinary text, with optional encryption on top.
entry.deeper_look:
SNOW is a small command-line steganography tool. It takes a message and appends spaces and tabs to the ends of lines in an ASCII text file. In most viewers those characters are invisible, so the text looks unchanged while carrying a payload. The name stands for the Steganographic Nature Of Whitespace.

The homepage presents it as concealment first and encryption second. The message can be encrypted with the built-in ICE algorithm, so even a reader who spots the trailing whitespace still faces ciphertext. In the author's words: "Locating trailing whitespace in text is like finding a polar bear in a snowstorm."

The idea underneath is that hiding is different from encrypting. Encryption makes a message unreadable but obviously present, while steganography tries to hide that a message exists at all. Whitespace is a good place to look because nobody reads it, and it is also why diff tools, editors, and linters that strip trailing spaces can destroy such a message. That makes it a quick way into questions about covert channels and how text gets handled.

The project is old. The newest source on the homepage is dated 2013, and the page also carries a 1998 history of encryption bugs that were fixed. The homepage also links a JavaScript version and a CGI script that hides messages in HTML pages, though I could not follow those links.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the usage summary, so you can see the options for concealing and extracting a message and for setting a password.

entry.whats_unique: It hides data in trailing whitespace, which almost nobody inspects, and pairs that with a real cipher so a discovered message is still unreadable.
entry.caveats: The project is old: the newest source is from 2013, and I could not check the manual page or the 'How it works' page, so the exact encoding and flags are unverified here.
